Synopsis:
    The UK recorded its hottest summer since 1884, with a mean temperature of 16.5°C, marking the second consecutive record-breaking summer. The season brought widespread drought, an unprecedented number of wildfires, and the worst cereal harvest since 1984. Climate attribution science links the event to human-induced climate change, making such summers ~130x more likely. Mainland Europe suffered more severely, with heatwaves causing fatalities and power supply disruptions.
